description: This pie chart represents the relative share of the most frequent languages in a dataset, displaying a total of 10 categories. The chart does not use a separate legend; instead, the language labels are positioned around the outer perimeter, while the corresponding percentage values are located inside each slice. The segments are visually ordered in a counter-clockwise direction starting from the top left, arranged by descending size and represented by a monochromatic color scale that transitions from dark to light blue. The largest segment is "English" in dark blue at 42.8%, followed by "Spanish" in a medium blue at 31.4%. Continuing counter-clockwise, the slices progressively decrease in size and lighten in shade: "Russian" (5.7%), "German" (3.6%), "French" (2.9%), "Chinese" (2.5%), "Thai" (1.9%), "Portuguese (Brazil)" (1.7%), and "Catalan" (1.6%). The sequence concludes at the top right with the "Other" category, which is depicted in the lightest pale blue and accounts for 5.8% of the total, breaking the strict descending size order. No individual slices are visually emphasized by being exploded or offset, though the font sizes of the text labels generally scale with the size of their respective segments.
